course_description:
This course introduces Biotechnology Honours Students to a framework called The Commercialization Tourbillon that can be used to assess the future and potential commercialisation feasibility of their research.

An important aspect of biotechnology is understanding the process of how bio-based discoveries are brought to market. This course focuses on the production of knowledge, goods, and services aspect of biotechnology, specifically the commercialisation of research. In this applied, interactive course Biotechnology Honours students will be introduced to the 12-steps of the Commercialization Tourbillon framework and apply it to assess the commercialisation feasibility of a potential biotechnology product, process, or service, including the underpinning intellectual property, its value, market opportunity, pathways to market, financial viability, and future horizons, that could emanate from a research project, preferably their honours research project.

course_aims: The course aims to provide students with an understanding of how to assess the commercialisation feasibility of a potential biotechnology product using the 12-step Commercialization Tourbillon framework. Students will lean about each step in the framework and apply it to an early stage research project to identify potential products and develop an understanding of how, or even if, this product could be or should be developed and commercialised. Included in this is developing an appreciation for commercial and non-commercial value that research and biotechnology products could provide.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand and apply the concept of intellectual property and the need for its protection and management, including commercialisation.
Analyse and evaluate the need to build a strategy for protecting and exploiting IP, which leads to a commercially or non-commercially focussed outcome.
Apply, analyse and evaluate the basic principles and alternative steps of taking commercial and non-commercial research to their audience.
Create paths to commercialisation based upon decision making regarding IP profiles, portfolios and business objectives.

Communicate the strategic paths to commercialisation based upon decision making regarding IP profiles, portfolios and business objectives, including alternative steps of taking commercial and non-commercial research to their audience.

learning_activities.topic: Introductory Lecture Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Steps 1 & 2 - Viability Public/Private Goods Matrix & Commercial and Societal Value of biotechnology products, processes, and services. Learning outcomes: L02, L03
Steps 3 - 5 - IP The need for Intellectual Property (IP) protection, IP protection mechanisms, IP management considerations. Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Steps 6 & 7 - Development & Support Planning development cycles, technology readiness levels, and strategic alliances. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04
Steps 8 & 9 - Markets & Competitors Understanding and anaysing market opportunities and competitive threats. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04
Steps 10 - 12 - Futures & Finance Evaluating strategic pathways, future horizons, and financial viability. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05
Bringing it all together Iterating the Tourbillon, communicating and justifying outcomes, and preparing to present. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 9 To Week 11
learning_activities.topic: Workshopping the Tourbillon Formal lectures will wrap up in week 8. In weeks 9, 10 and 11, students are encouraged to attend class and use this time to ask questions, ahead of their draft report submission. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
